1.Nf3 d5 2.g3 c6 3.Bg2 Nf6 4.O-O Bf5 5.d.strategy: Blocks the bishop's diagonal on d3, where the pawn is guarded several times, and controls e4 so the bishop loses its hold there. White keeps a solid structure, frees the c1-bishop and prepares to bring out the b1 knight.

Reinforces d5 with a second pawn and opens the way for the dark-squared bishop. With the light-squared bishop already outside the chain, the e6 pawn buries no piece, and Black gets a solid, compact set-up.
Takes g5 away from White's pieces and gives the bishop a retreat on h7 if White harasses it. It costs a tempo on the kingside while White goes on developing, but the bishop keeps its active diagonal.
